sentences.text: The petitioners - accused herein who are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 504, 323 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act are before this Court.

The case of the prosecution is that, the accused No.1 is the husband, accused No.2 is the mother- in-law, accused No.3 is the sister-in-law and accused No.4 is the husband of accused No.3 and they have subjected the de facto complainant to cruelty both physically and mentally and a demand was made to bring money from the parental house.
3.
Accused No.1 had filed a petition under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for dissolving his marriage with the de facto complainant on the ground of cruelty.

In the said proceedings, accused No.1 entered into a settlement with the de facto complainant and as per the terms of settlement , the marriage of accused No.1 with the de facto complainant has been dissolved and a sum of Rs.4,08,000/- was paid towards permanent alimony and respondent No.2 -de facto complainant has no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings.

4. Though the offences alleged are cognizable and non-compoundable, however, having heard the fact that NC: 2023:KHC:29060 the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves in M.C.No.1896/2020 and respondent No.2 having no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings, it would be a futile exercise, if the accused are subjected to trial since the probability of the conviction of accused is remote.
Hence, the continuation of the criminal proceeding would be an abuse of process of law.

Hence, the following order:
(i) The criminal petition is allowed.
(ii) The impugned order in C.C.NO.51325/2021 on the file of XI Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Mayo Hall at Bangalore is hereby quashed.
In view of disposal of the petition, pending I.A. does not survive for consideration.
